text:
linda: quick sync — we've been talking about the long-term plan to peel apart the session mesh and reduce the hotpath debt. i sketched a conservative migration that keeps the runtime hotpath intact but extracts an enrichment corridor. thoughts?

arjun: love the conservative approach. can you paste the sketch? curious about ownership of kv-cache and prefix caching — major risk vector.

linda: pasted below, very rough. main ideas: 1) extract enrichment worker service (async) 2) keep the runtime for hot inference + cache reads 3) move writes and enrichments behind a sidecar with well defined API 4) gradual traffic split via flags

linda: ```
# sketch
Runtime (hot) -> Forwarder -> Enricher (new svc, async)
- runtime continues to own KV read cache
- enrichments write to durable store and notify forwarder when ready
- forwarder exposes small sync API for callers that need immediate enrichment (falls back to runtime cached stub)
```

matt: sounds reasonable. two quick tradeoffs: 1) increases tail latency for callers that require enrichment unless we do sync paths 2) introduces eventual consistency cases we need to own in UX and docs

sara: for the cache: i'd prefer runtime remain authoritative for reads but enforcer owns eviction policy configs. runtime should call a control-plane API for policy, not storage. keeps path fast.

arjun: +1 for read-only runtime. eviction policy as config makes sense. also: what about canarying? do we want shadow writes first or direct split?

linda: plan: shadow writes for 2 weeks (traffic mirrored), then 5% canary, 25%, 50% roll. rollback path at each stage.

pm-ellen: quick product note — some enterprise customers rely on deterministic enrichment order (regulatory). we need a compatibility mode that guarantees synchronous ordering for flagged tenants.

jessie: ops-bot: create runbook placeholder for "enricher cutover" and add postmortem template

ops-bot: runbook created: #enricher-cutover-runbook (link: https://wiki.redwood/enricher-cutover) :white_check_mark:

kevin: data migration question — enrichments currently appended to session blob in place. new model writes per-enrichment objects. how do we reconcile history queries?

linda: two options: 1) backfill writer that compacts old blobs into per-enrichment rows (costly) 2) read-path adapter that enumerates blob contents and emits synthetic rows on-the-fly (cheap but runtime overhead). leaning to #2 initially.

matt: agree with #2 for initial rollout. add background compaction on low-usage tenants as followup.

arjun: instrumentation: we need new metrics: enrichment-lag, forwarder-error-rate, cache-hit-after-fallback. add sampling of out-of-order requests for SLA audit.

sara: also add a quality-regression alert tied to our eval runner — if enrichment output distribution drifts, auto-pause canary.

linda: noted. i'll add the list to the RFC follow-up doc.

pm-ellen: timeline ask from me: can we get first shadow stage within 8 weeks? customers are start-of-quarter sensitive.

linda: that feels tight but doable if we scope to single region + opt-in tenants only. prioritizing infra and a minimal API surface.

jessie: patch-level checklist request: feature-flag gate, async queue (idempotent), replay id in event, idempotency token, migration adapter for reads, test harness.

kevin: security note — new service must accept only signed internal JWTs and we need a short-lived key rotation plan. add to design.

arjun: let's not forget SLA mapping — if enrichment moves async, some clients will need a contractual SLA for enriched results. need PM/legal input.

pm-ellen: flagged. i'll get legal looped for enterprise contract implications.

matt: one more practical thing — add a debug endpoint on forwarder to surface blob->enrichment mapping for support. secured behind admin auth.

sara: agree. and instrument distribution of enrichment durations; helps the canary health checks.

linda: good. i'll produce a condensed checklist and assign owners. proposal: 8-week shadow -> 4-week 5% canary -> 3-week ramp -> compaction cadence starts after 6 months.

arjun: can we add a technical KPI: tech debt points removed = number of hotpath lines removed + % requests now routed off-hotpath? helps quantify paydown.

matt: +1. define measurement method in the RFC. also include expected cost delta per token for first 3 months.

jessie: i'll own the runbook and rollback playbook. kevin takes security. sara takes observability. arjun + linda own runtime guardrails. pm-ellen owns enterprise compatibility mode.

linda: thanks team. i'll post the RFC follow-up with checklist and owners by EOD tomorrow. small ask: if you have concerns about the read-adapter vs backfill choice, drop them in the doc — we should decide before shadow.

kevin: noted one more PR: add JWK endpoint to control plane and rotate keys weekly for initial rollout.

matt: :thumbsup:

ops-bot: reminder: weekly architecture sync scheduled on Tue 10:00am. added "enricher cutover" to agenda.

linda: awesome — see y'all Tue. thanks for quick feedback!
